name: Influencer Hero
summary: All-in-one influencer marketing platform: AI creator discovery, automated outreach, an influencer CRM, UGC tracking and affiliate management on one record per creator, with 45-plus native integrations and payouts run through bank debit at 0.1-0.4% rather than 2-3% card fees. Every plan carries the full toolset — the ladder is gated on quota and seats. A reach-out is counted once when a new influencer is first contacted — all later messaging with that creator is unlimited. Three-month minimum on every plan and no free trial.
best_for: brands running influencer marketing as a continuous programme rather than a campaign, with enough volume to use 1,000 reach-outs a month from the first month, who want discovery, outreach, a creator CRM, UGC tracking and affiliate management in one place instead of a spreadsheet plus four tools
skip_if: you want to test the channel before committing, because the three-month minimum makes the real entry price $1,557 rather than $519, or you are a two-person team on Standard's single seat. Skip Standard if you pay more than 20 creators a month; Pro raises the cap to 200
honest_knock:
The three-month minimum is the real commitment, and there is no free trial to soften it. Every plan carries it, so the smallest honest entry price is not $519 but three months — $1,557 on the quarterly rate, $1,947 if you pay monthly. An influencer programme takes longer than four weeks to show you anything, so the vendor is not being unreasonable; it just means the decision is a quarter of spending rather than a month of trying.

Read which column you are quoted. The public pricing page leads with the quarterly rate, so $519 is what gets repeated — but billed monthly the same plan is $649, a quarter more. Pro is $839 or $1,049, Business $1,992 or $2,490. The 20% and 30% savings are genuine and check out exactly against the monthly rate; the trap is only that the advertised number already has the discount in it.

What the ladder actually meters is worth understanding, because it is better than it looks. A reach-out counts once, at the moment you first contact a new influencer. Every follow-up, reply and ongoing conversation with that same creator after that is unlimited and never draws the quota down again — so the meter counts new relationships opened, not messages sent. Standard's 1,000 a month is therefore 1,000 new creators, which is a great many, and nurturing the ones who answer costs nothing.

Hitting the cap gives you two routes and the vendor recommends one of them against its own short-term interest: buy a top-up, or move up a tier. Their own documentation says brands who top up once tend to keep doing it, so repeated top-ups erode the saving from staying low. No top-up rate is published anywhere, which is the one number still missing from an otherwise unusually open account.

Payouts are capped per plan, and the cap is what pushes paying brands up the ladder: 20 a month on Standard, 200 on Pro, 500 on Business and unlimited only on Enterprise. The Business card briefly said unlimited after a site revamp; the vendor corrected it, and on 24 September 2026 the pricing page gave 500 on both the card and the comparison grid.

Seats follow the quota — one, three, eight — so a two-person team is pushed to Pro by headcount alone, whatever its volume.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month, or $454 a month billed annually (also $519 billed quarterly)
pricing.notes:
(pricing matrix read 18 September 2026 in documentation the vendor sent us; the public ladder at influencer-hero.com/pricing was read the same week and shows the quarterly column) Four plans, and the figure you see depends entirely on the billing term you pick. Billed monthly: Standard $649, Pro $1,049, Business $2,490. Billed quarterly: $519, $839 and $1,992 — and this is the column the public pricing page leads with, which is why $519 is the number most people quote. Billed annually: $454, $734 and $1,743. The advertised 20% and 30% savings check out exactly against the monthly rate ($649 × 0.8 = $519.20, × 0.7 = $454.30), so the discounts are real and the headline is simply the discounted one.

What each plan carries: Standard is one seat, 1,000 reach-outs a month and 20 influencer payouts. Pro is three seats, 5,000 reach-outs and 200 payouts. Business is eight seats, 10,000 reach-outs and 500 payouts, and Enterprise has unlimited payouts. On 19 September the Business plan card still said unlimited while the comparison grid on the same page said 500; Influencer Hero told us the card was a leftover from a site revamp, and when we re-read the page on 24 September 2026 the card and the grid both said 500 for Business and unlimited for Enterprise. Enterprise is custom on every other axis. Every plan carries a three-month minimum term and there is no free trial, so the smallest real commitment is three months of Standard: $1,947 billed monthly, or $1,557 if you take the quarterly rate. The influencer CRM, the outreach automation and the UGC tracking are in every plan; the ladder is gated on quota and seats. Influencer payouts can run through bank direct debit (ACH in the US, Bacs in the UK, SEPA in the EU) with only Stripe's processing fee passed through: 0.1% to 0.4% by the vendor's own account, around 0.4% to 0.5% effective by its Payout Manager post, with US ACH capped at $5 a payout, against the 2-3% that card processors typically charge.

compare_with.name: Superfiliate, Stamped
compare_with.why:
The useful comparison in this category is who will tell you the price. Superfiliate, from our own dossier (re-checked 5 September 2026), publishes none at all: superfiliate.com/pricing returns a 404, there is no pricing item in the navigation, and the only call to action is Book Demo — its Shopify listing publishes the shape rather than the amount. Against that, Influencer Hero putting $519, $839 and $1,992 on a public page with the quotas attached is the more respectful treatment of a buyer, and it is the reason a fair write-up is even possible.

Stamped is the other end and a different job: reviews, loyalty and repeat purchasing rather than creator outreach, priced on your monthly order volume (re-verified 12 September 2026) — Reviews at $23 a month at the 200-order step, $199 at 5,000 orders, Loyalty $299, Repeat $499, and a multi-product bundle at a flat $798. If what you actually want is more from the customers you already have, that ladder starts an order of magnitude lower than this one. Influencer Hero is for going and finding people who have not bought from you yet, and the three-month minimum says the vendor knows that takes a while.
